<p>The amendment was therefore negatived.</p>

<speech by="#fitzpatrick">

<from><span class="col_1277-1278" refersTo="page_0648"/>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. P. FITZPATRICK</person> (Pretoria East)</from>

<p>said if they were always to divide upon this subject of translation, they would find themselves in a very difficult position. He suggested before putting a clause where there was a word in the English that had no corresponding equivalent in the Dutch, they should leave the word out, so that the two versions might agree.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#cronje">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. R. CRONJE</person> (Winburg)</from>

<p>moved that the word &#x201C;ongeoorloofd&#x201D; be inserted in front of &#x201C;gemeenschap.&#x201D; (Opposition laughter.)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#botha">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. L. BOTHA</person> (Bloemfontein) (laughing):</from>

<p>Well, I accept that.</p>

<p>The amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>The clause, as amended, was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 34,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>moved to insert the word &#x201C;knowingly&#x201D; before the word &#x201C;suffers.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#smartt">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. W. SMARTT</person> (For Beaufort)</from>

<p>drew attention to the extraordinary differences in the marginal notes of the two versions.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he was beginning to think there was a good deal behind all these amendements. (Ministerial cheers.) He was exceedingly sorry that the matter had been raised, because it was very evident that in English some part of the sentence had been left out in committee. If the hon. member would simply draw attention to any mistake, they would be only too glad to assist him in any way, but he was exceedingly sorry that there had been an evidence in this comparison of the two languages that afternoon and the day before to arouse a feeling&#x2014; (Cries of &#x201C;No, no.&#x201D;)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#smartt">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. W. SMARTT</person> (Fort Beaufort)</from>

<p>he regretted extremely that his hon. friend (General Hertzog) should approach this subject in the manner he did. &#x2018;That attitude would not facilitate the business of the House. (Hear, hear.) He denied most emphatically, on behalf of those on that side of the House, that it was their intention to try and arouse any comparison between the merits of the two languages. They were only trying to do their duty in connection with these differences. Were they to understand that when a Minister was dealing with a Bill with clauses that were not understood that hon. members were not allowed an opportunity of seeing that, as far as possible, the two versions were correct? That was all they asked for. Hon. members would recollect that although English was the official language in the old Cape Parliament, there was always a translation in Dutch, and if the two versions did not correspond, hon. members drew attention to the fact. Their only purpose in pointing out these discrepancies was to see that both versions were correct, and he did not think it was the duty of a responsible Minister to take up the position that his hon. friend had. (Hear, hear.) Surely it was their duty, especially when people outside the House were commenting upon these discrepancies, that they should point them out. What they wanted the Minister to do was, whenever there was a difference in the two versions, he would see that it was put right, but he (Sir T. Smartt) must protest against the insinuation that they were trying to make the dual language impossible. All they wanted was that the dual language should be maintained, so that anybody reading either one or the other language would know exactly what was intended. The hon. member regretted that his night hon. friend the Prime Minister was not present, because he would not have taken up the same attitude as the Minister of Justice. (Hear, hear.) He made certain allowances for the hon. member&#x2019;s attitude, because, perhaps, he bad been a little bit annoyed at criticisms directed against the Bill, but he had no right to insinuate that hon. members were not doing their duty when they pointed out irregularities. (Hear, hear.)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watermeyer">

<from>&#x2020; Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. B. WATERMEYER</person> (Clanwilliam)</from>

<p>said that he must admit that they, as members of Parliament, had a duty to perform in regard to the two languages. It was true that, as he had found, one language give the same sense as the other, but the terms were not exactly the same, and he had been considering whether they had been doing their duty. With all due deference he appealed to the Minister of Justice to see that they&#x2014;on both sides of the House&#x2014;were so careful that nothing should be placed on the Statute Book, the two versions of which might differ greatly from each other.</p>

<p>The amendment moved by Mr. Jagger was agreed to, and the clause was adopted.</p>

<p>On clause 35. Jurisdiction of superintendents to try breach of regulations by convicts,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>moved in sub-section (b) to insert after &#x201C;privileges&#x201D; the word &#x201C;gratuities.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis)</from>

<p>oved an amendment to omit sub-section (e), which give a superintendent power to inflict corporal punishment not exceeding six strokes if the offender be a convicted male prisoner apparently under the age of sixty years. He also proposed the omission of sub-section (g), which give power to a superintendent to order solitary confinement in an isolation cell, with or without light labour, for a period not exceeding 21 days, 14 days of which might be ordered to be passed on reduced diet.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#berry">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. B. BERRY</person> (Queenstown)</from>

<p>said he had been a visitor to gaols, and be had seen isolation cells of a kind which would make General Hertzog&#x2019;s hair stand on end. To give any superintendent <span class="col_1279-1280" refersTo="page_0649"/>power to! send any person to one of these horrible dens for 21 days was monstrous. He had seen a man brought out from one of these isolation cells, and the horrible expression on the man&#x2019;s face when again he saw the light of day had remained impressed on his (Sir Bisset&#x2019;s) memory. There were very few isolation cells in the country fit for the purpose for which they were intended. He moved in line 21, after &#x201C;cell&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;approved of by the director,&#x201D; and in line 25 after &#x201C;cell&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;approved of by the director or medical officer of health.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that if the hon. member (Sir Bisset Berry) had considered the words of the whole of the clause, he would have seen that the amendment was superfluous. He sympathised with hon. members who held that, if possible, they should take all kinds of punishment out of the hands of gaolers. In the Transvaal many of the punishments were double those provided for in the section, and were in the hands of governors or deputy-governors. The operation of this, clause would be restricted to places where they had proper isolation cells.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#berry">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. B. BERRY</person> (Queen&#x2019;s Town)</from>

<p>said that the Minister seemed to have misunderstood him. His point was that the isolation cell should be approved by the Director.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that provision was made for this in section 24. In regard to Mr. Nathan&#x2019;s amendments, he thought there was need to give jurisdiction to both the superintendent and assistant superintendent. The power would only be given where the exigencies of the case required. He had not much sympathy with the power referred to in sub-section (e), and he would not mind if that portion were deleted. As to the proposal to substitute &#x201C;two&#x201D; for &#x201C;six&#x201D; days, in regard to sub-section (f), it was a matter about, which different, people held different views. In the Transvaal seven days was the maximum. He saw no objection to that amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>hoped that the Minister would stick to his clause, which was a very good one. It was necessary to inflict some corporal punishment in certain very bad or obstreperous cases.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly)</from>

<p>thought that a medical officer should be consulted before a prisoner was sentenced to reduced or spare diet.</p>

<p>Verbal amendments by the Minister of Justice and by Mr. E. Nathan were agreed to.</p>

<p>Those by Sir B. Berry were withdrawn.</p>

<p>Others by Mr. E. Nathan were negatived.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watermeyer">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. B. WATERMEYER</person> (Calvinia)</from>

<p>moved certain amendments in sub-section (g) in the Dutch version, so as to make it correspond more with the English version.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>suggested the words &#x201C;op bevel&#x201D; instead.</p>

<p>Business was suspended at 6 p.m.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#evening_sitting">

<heading>EVENING SITTING.</heading>

<p>Business was resumed at 8 p.m.</p>

<p>The amendment in the Dutch by the Minister of Justice was agreed to, and one by Mr. P. J. G. Theron was, withdrawn.</p>

<p>On clause 36, jurisdiction of magistrates to try breaches of regulations by convicts or prisoners,</p>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>moved to insert at the beginning of the clause, &#x201C;save as is otherwise provided in this Act.&#x201D; This amendment, he said, was necessary, in order to bring the clause into harmony with clause 27, as amended.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>thought it would be better to add &#x201C;subject to the provisions of section 27.&#x201D; He moved accordingly.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>said he would agree to that, and withdrew his amendment.</p>

<p>The amendment was agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis) moved:</from>

<p>In line 37, to omit, &#x201C;unless the Minister otherwise direct, either generally or specially,&#x201D; and to add at, the end of the clause, &#x201C;provided that such visiting magistrate or magistrates, as the case may be, shall not try or hear such cases in a, prison or gaol where the trial or hearing can be had in an open court of law.&#x201D; As it stood, the clause, he said, was very vague. They should make it clear what, powers they were going to give the authorities, and what the power the Minister was to retain.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he considered the clause provided the best means of dealing with the matter, pointing out the difficulties there would be in removing convicts from gaols to courts to be sentenced for small contraventions, if the amendment were agreed to. The clause was based on the Transvaal Act of 1906.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>said that he could not agree with the hon. member for Von Brandis (Mr. Nathan), who was asking too much. He thought they must leave power to the authorities to deal with small contraventions, such as insubordination in gaol. He thought his hon. friend (Mr. Nathan) should be satisfied with the provision that had been made to have the more serious cases dealt with in open court.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#alexander">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">M. ALEXANDER</person> (Cape Town, Castle)</from>

<p>moved that the words, &#x201C;and shall have the following special jurisdiction,&#x201D; be inserted in line 44, and the deletion of the words, &#x201C;to sentence the offender in lieu of.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_railways_and_harbours">

<from><span class="col_1281-1282" refersTo="page_0650"/>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND HARBOURS</person></from>

<p>said that the magistrate could give the first sentence, the second, or both.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that there was no question of a man being sentenced twice.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person></from>

<p>&#x2019;s amendment was negatived.</p>

<p>The amendment of the Minister of Justice was agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that with regard to the question of collective sentences, hon. members on the other side assumed that the man had already been tried.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#meyler">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. M. MEYLER</person> (Weenen)</from>

<p>asked which version of the Bill would be signed by the Governor-General? If the English version was to be laid before the Governor-General, they need not trouble about the Dutch translation.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person></from>

<p>ruled that the question was not before the committee.</p>

<p>The clause as amended was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 37, review of sentences for prison offences by a judge.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#alexander">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">M. ALEXANDER</person> (Gape Town),</from>

<p>Castle moved that the words, &#x201C;or solitary confinement&#x201D; be inserted after the word &#x201C;punishment&#x201D; in line 66.</p>

<p>The amendment was lost.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis)</from>

<p>said that the punishment in clause 36 was very severe, therefore he moved to omit the words &#x201C;and 36&#x201D; from paragraph 3.</p>

<p>The amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>The clause as amended was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 38, jurisdiction of superintendents,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis) moved the following amendment:</from>

<p>In paragraph (1) to omit the whole of line 6, and substitute the word &#x201C;A &#x201D;; in paragraph (2), line 16, to omit &#x201C;whether&#x201D; and to substitute &#x201C;either.&#x201D; He pointed out that a prisoner who sought to gain some advantage from his superior officer might give evidence which might be to the detriment of the person charged, and advantage to the person giving evidence. Why could not these cases be brought before a Magistrate? All he wished to do was to obviate the possibility of any injustice being done.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#brown">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D. M. BROWN</person> (Three Rivers)</from>

<p>considered that the accused should have the right to appeal to the Minister.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he was prepared to insert after the word &#x201C;director,&#x201D; in line 14, the words may with the approval of the Minister.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Mr. Nathan&#x2019;s amendments were negatived.</p>

<p>The amendments proposed by the Minister of Justice were agreed to.</p>

<p>The clause as amended was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 39,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#struben">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. F. W. STRUBEN</person> (Newlands)</from>

<p>moved an amendment in effect to allow any person awaiting trial an opportunity of obtaining legal advice.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>said if the suggestion were for the benefit of the legal profession he would have much pleasure in supporting it. (Laughter.)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that any man awaiting trial in gaol who wanted a lawyer was allowed to have one.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis)</from>

<p>said the amendment proposed by his hon. friend was quite unnecessary. (Laughter.) His (Mr. Nathan&#x2019;s) went far enough.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town. Central)</from>

<p>suggested that the clause should stand over.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he was ready to do that, as he wished to consult additional authorities. He moved accordingly.</p>

<p>The clause was ordered to stand over.</p>

<p>On clause 40,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis) moved:</from>

<p>To add to paragraph (2), line 34, after &#x201C;Court&#x201D; the following: &#x201C;Provided, however, that the accused shall in all cases at any hearing be entitled to have present and be represented by his legal adviser.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#struben">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. F. W. STRUBEN</person> (Newlands) moved:</from>

<p>In line 32, after &#x201C;thereat,&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;or be the legal representative duly authorised by the person or persons charged,&#x201D; and to add the following new sub-section, viz.: &#x201C;3. Any person so charged shall, for the purposes of such trial, be allowed full liberty to communicate with, receive visits from, and be represented by such qualified practitioner as he may be disposed.&#x201D;</p>

<p>After discussion,</p>

<p>On the motion of the MINISTER OF JUSTICE, the further consideration of this clause was ordered to stand over.</p>

<p>On clause 41,</p>

<p>An amendment was made in the Dutch which does not occur in the English version.</p>

<p>On clause 43, return to prison of persons removed there from on account of insanity,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis)</from>

<p>moved to add at the end of the clause: &#x201C;Provided, however, that the case of such convict or prisoner and all the attendant facts shall forthwith be brought by the person in charge of such convict or prisoner to the notice of the Governor-General for the exercising of his prerogative if by him deemed advisable,&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from><span class="col_1283-1284" refersTo="page_0651"/>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Gape Town, Central)</from>

<p>said he hoped the Minister would accept this very reasonable amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that a safeguard was provided by means of the Prison Board. Besides, the gaoler would have to submit a prison list to the Magistrate. It seemed to him that they had safeguarded by the provisions of the Bill against any injustice being done. Any prisoner could send a petition at any time to the Governor or to himself (the Minister of Justice).</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis)</from>

<p>said that the amendment made it perfectly clear that a man&#x2019;s case Should not be over looked. The clause said that &#x201C;the period during which he was detained in the asylum shall not be reckoned as part of his sentence of imprisonment.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that he would be prepared to accept the amendment if the words &#x201C;by the person in charge of such convict or prisoner&#x201D; were omitted, and &#x201C;Minister&#x201D; was substituted for &#x201C;Governor-General.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nathan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. NATHAN</person> (Von Brandis)</from>

<p>amended his motion to this effect, and the amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 51,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#clayton">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. F. CLAYTON</person> (Zululand)</from>

<p>moved a new clause 51 as follows: &#x201C;Where any person, is convicted of an offence before any Court, and the Court is of opinion that it is inexpedient to pass sentence of imprisonment, the Court may direct (a) That the accused be remitted to the magistrate of the district within which his home is situate, who shall indenture him to an employer for industrial service within such district, for a period not exceeding five years, and shall determine the conditions of service and rate of wages to be paid to the parent or guardian of the accused (if he or she be less than 21 years of age), or to be deposited with the magistrate to the credit of the accused (if he or she be an adult), in which latter case the magistrate may at his discretion pay over to the accused a sum not exceeding one-half of the wages in hand at any time, the balance being paid over at the expiry of the period of service, (b) Further direct that a portion of the wages to be paid under the preceding paragraph be retained by the magistrate by way of fine payable to the Court, and/or of damages caused to the complainant by the offence of which the accused has been convicted.&#x201D; He said there were many occasions on which a Judge or a Magistrate did not wish to send a first offender or a person not of vicious tendencies to prison, or to a reformatory. He wished to give the Magistrates power to deal with such cases otherwise. The tendency of all legislation was in this direction, and he hoped the amendment would&#x2019; be accepted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that no doubt there was a good deal to be said for such a provision, but it was foreign to the present Bill. The questions treated in the proposed new clause were dealt with by existing legislation in the different Provinces, which legislation was not here being repealed. In so far as any crime was dealt with here, it was confined to crimes committed in a gaol. The new clause would be quite in place when they came to deal with the criminal law next year, but it was out of place here.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#clayton">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. F. CLAYTON</person> (Zululand)</from>

<p>said that, in regard to the matter of apprenticeships, this clause would fall within the provisions of this Bill.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>referred to clause 2, and said he could see no difference in principle between this proposed new clause and clause 2.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that the Bill did not deal with the general criminal law. It dealt with a special kind of criminal.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>said that the principle contained in the amendment was in operation in other countries. The suggestion had this merit, that it relieved the State of the necessity of caring for these offenders. It was true &#x2018;that the State would have to exercise some supervision, but so far as the question of care and provision was concerned, the Government was not called upon for one penny. He hoped that if the Minister would not accept the amendment that night, he would at all events allow it to stand over, as there was a great deal in it worth considering. As regarded the amendment itself, he found fault with it in so far as it said &#x201C;that the accused be remitted to the magistrate of the district within which his home is situate.&#x2019;&#x2019; He considered that the district in which the accused&#x2019;s home was situated was the last place to which he should be sent. Instead of sending him back to the place of temptation, he should be sent to a new atmosphere and new surroundings.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he was quite willing to allow the clause to stand over.</p>

<p>Tine clause was allowed to stand over accordingly.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#clayton">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. F. CLAYTON</person> (Zululand)</from>

<p>moved: That the following be a new clause, viz: &#x201C;52. Any person who may be dealt with under the preceding section shall be considered as coming within the operation of the <b>Master and Servants Act</b> of the Province within which he is resident, and shall, if occasion require, be dealt with there under.</p>

<p>On the motion of the MINISTER OF JUSTICE, the further consideration of this clause was ordered to Stand over.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#clayton">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. F. CLAYTON</person> (Zululand)</from>

<p>moved that the following be a new clause, viz.: <span class="col_1285-1286" refersTo="page_0652"/>&#x201C;53. The Governor of any gaol or prison may recommend to the Minister having jurisdiction that the course laid down in the foregoing sub-section (a) of section be followed in respect of any prisoner whose conduct warrants such modification of the sentence of imprisonment originally inflicted, and the Minister may at his discretion direct that the prisoner be so dealt with.&#x201D;</p>

<p>On the motion of the MINISTER OF JUSTICE, the further consideration of this clause was ordered to stand over.</p>

<p>On clause 52, establishment of reformatories for juvenile offenders,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#berry">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. B. BERRY</person> (Queen&#x2019;s Town)</from>

<p>moved in paragraph (1), line 43, after &#x201C;reformatories,&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;in which term shall be included detention schools, as well as training ships afloat in territorial waters.&#x201D; He said that these young children should be sent to schools instead of being sent to a reformatory. They should not be allowed to be tainted by prison. Magistrates had often commented on the fact that there was no proper place where they could send these youthful offenders. In dealing with the question of training ships, he said that he hoped he would have the support of the committee. The subject was mooted in the old Cape House some years back, but he believed that the objection to the proposal arose from the fact that it &#x2018;was only &#x2018;being done with the idea of denationalising the youth of this country. He considered that the results would be worth the expense of establishing such ships. He thought that even the young criminals would prefer going to a training ship than a convict station, and he did think the question one worth considering. He would draw the attention of the Minister of Justice that in a country like England, and it was the same in France and Germany, these training ships had now become well-known institutions. In most of the large seaports of England training ships were established. The Metropolitan Asylums Board and the London School Board had ships of this description on the Thames, and that was a wrinkle that he would draw the attention of his hon. friend (Mr. Jagger) to. He thought the time had arrived when they should establish one or two of these training ships. General Hertzsog pointed out that the Governor-General had the power to establish detention schools and training ships, but the amendment of the hon. member would abrogate that power. It did not matter whether they were called detention schools or reformatories, it was the same thing. The Hon. Minister give as an illustration what he would call a perfect system, the juvenile reformatory established at Heidelberg, which was based upon the American or cottage system.</p>

<p>There the boys were brought up just like a family, with the house father in charge. He did not think the hon. gentleman could wish for anything better. In substance this was the same as the hon. gentleman desired; then why put in an amendment?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person></from>

<p>thought the Governor-General&#x2019;s authority would be required if training ships were included in the Bill, as that would mean additional expenditure.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>urged the acceptance of the amendment, as it would open the door to getting a training ship. Someone might collect money for the purpose.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he had no objection to the portion of the amendment referring to training ships. (Opposition cheers.)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#berry">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. B. BERRY</person> (Queen&#x2019;s Town)</from>

<p>altered his amendment accordingly.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he would, in the definition of reformatories, have training ships included. (Opposition cheers.)</p>

<p>The amendment was agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#duncan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">P. DUNCAN</person> (Fordsburg)</from>

<p>moved to odd at the end of paragraph (1): &#x201C;And may also establish reformatories for the reception and custody of juvenile adults &#x201D;; end to omit the word &#x201C;juvenile&#x201D; before&#x201D; reformatories&#x201D; or &#x201C;reformatory,&#x201D; whenever it occurred. He said that his object was to establish not only juvenile reformatories, but juvenile adult reformatories.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that this was provided for, though in a different way, in clause 73. He did not think there was any need to accept the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#duncan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">P. DUNCAN</person> (Fordsburg)</from>

<p>was of opinion that clause 73 was not the best way of arriving at the result. He had put on the paper a new clause 73.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said that there appeared to be a good deal in what the hon. member had said, and he would, therefore, not raise any objection to the amendment.</p>

<p>The amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>The clause, as amended, was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 53, convicted juvenile may, in addition to or in lieu of imprisonment, be sentenced to detention in reformatory or to apprenticeship,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#struben">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. F. W. STRUBEN</person> (Newlands)</from>

<p>said that he desired to introduce a new principle in reference to offences committed by young children. He thought a magistrate or other special officer should have the power to try such cases in camera. The principle had been adopted with success in England. He moved to add a sub-section to the effect that the trial of any such juvenile may in every <span class="col_1287-1288" refersTo="page_0653"/>case be held in camera, and in some other place than an ordinary court-room, provided that in such case the parent or guardian, or other person interested in such juvenile, should have the right to be present thereat.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he agreed with the principle, but there was just a danger in giving a privilege&#x2014;and a very good privilege&#x2014;and they must take care that it should not be &#x2018;abused. He moved that the clause stand over, as there seemed to be something wrong.</p>

<p>This was agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#smartt">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. W. SMARTT</person> (Fort Beaufort)</from>

<p>suggested that the Minister move to report progress.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>said he would like to meet the wish of the hon. member for Fort Beaufort, but he would point out that the other House was really having nothing to do. Besides, if they did not get on, he was afraid some very important measures would be hung up.</p>

<p>On clause 60, Visitors&#x2019; Board and other visitors,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>moved an amendment to the effect that ministers of religion should also be allowed to visit.</p>

<p>The amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>The clause, as amended, was agreed to.</p>

<p>Clause 65 having been agreed to,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>moved that progress be reported.</p>

<p>The motion was agreed to, and leave obtained to sit again on Monday.</p>

</speech>

<adjournment>

<p>The House adjourned at <recordedTime time="1911-02-17T22:51:00">10.51 p.m.</recordedTime></p>

</adjournment>
