<speech by="#venter">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. A. VENTER</person> (Wodhouse),</from>

<p>from M. Ferguson, Postal Department.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#van_heerden">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. H. VAN HEERDEN</person> (Cradock),</from>

<p>from W. R. D. Fynn, who served under the late Cape Government.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#nicholson">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">R. G. NICHOLSON</person> (Waterberg),</from>

<p>from residents of Waterberg, against the legalisation of marriages between European and coloured persons.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#long">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">B. K. LONG</person> (Liesbeek),</from>

<p>from Hester Fife, pension.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#keyter">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. G. KEYTER</person> (Ficksburg),</from>

<p>from the Municipality of Ficksburg, praying that further Asiatic immigration be stopped.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#grobler">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. N. GROBLER</person> (Edenburg),</from>

<p>similar petition from the Village Management Board, Waterkloof, O.F.S.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#reports_laed_on_table">

<heading>REPORTS LAED ON TABLE</heading>

<speech by="#minister_of_public_works">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS</person>:</from>

<p>For construction of wagon-bridge over the Vaal River, at Paris.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_the_interior">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF THE INTERIOR</person>:</from>

<p>First and second reports of the Commission appointed for the reorganisation of the Departments of the Public Service.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_public_works">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS</person>:</from>

<p>Papers and contracts having reference to the erection of the Union Buildings in Pretoria.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#railways_and_harbours_service_bill_first_reading">

<heading>RAILWAYS AND HARBOURS SERVICE BILL<br/>FIRST READING</heading>

<p>The Bill was read a first time, and the second reading set down for Wednesday, 8th March.</p>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#public_debt_commissioners_bill_first_reading">

<heading>PUBLIC DEBT COMMISSIONERS BILL<br/>FIRST READING</heading>

<p>The Bill was read a first time, and the second reading set down for Wednesday.</p>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#master&#x2019;s_office_at_kimberley">

<heading>MASTER&#x2019;S OFFICE AT KIMBERLEY</heading>

<speech by="#oliver">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. A. OLIVER</person> (Kimberley)</from>

<p>moved that the petition from W. Gasson, Mayor, and 2,739 others, residents of Kimberley, against the proposed abolition of the Master&#x2019;s Office, Kimberley, presented to the House on February 22, 1911, be referred to the Government for consideration.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly)</from>

<p>seconded.</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#mines_works_machinery_and_certificates_bill">

<heading>MINES, WORKS, MACHINERY, AND CERTIFICATES BILL.</heading>

<p>In committee,</p>

<p>On clause 4, Power of Governor-General to make regulations as to mines, works, and machinery,</p>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said it was very dangerous to hand over large powers to Government to be used in the making of regulations. The principles and limitations of Government&#x2019;s power in the matter should clearly be set forth in the Bill. It was very necessary that there should be some chain, of responsibility.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chaplin">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. D. P. CHAPLIN</person> (Germiston):</from>

<p>Is the hon. member in order in discussing regulations not before the committee?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person>:</from>

<p>The hon. member is quite in order.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_mines">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF MINES</person>:</from>

<p>The hon. member is going further. He is discussing specific regulations which cannot be framed until the Bill is passed.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe):</from>

<p>I am most anxious not to transgress in any way, but T understood from the Minister that he had no objection to our discussing these things.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person>:</from>

<p>The hon. member must confine himself to the clause under consideration.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe):</from>

<p>I protest against the Bill being discussed until the regulations are laid before the House.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>moved that progress be reported, and leave obtained to sit again. It was only fair, he said, that the House should know exactly what it was doing in this matter. Most drastic and exclusive powers were given to the Minister under the Bill, and there was no reason why the House and the people should not know what they were doing in this matter. (Opposition cheers.) It was only a fair request that the Bill should stand over until the draft regulations were before the House. (Opposition cheers.) That course would not entail the loss of any time, as there was plenty of business on the paper. (Hear, hear.)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>suggested that the regulations should stand over, and the committee proceed with the rest of the Bill. (Hear, hear.) He also suggested that the regulations should be referred to a Select Committee.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Cape Town, Central)</from>

<p>said it might be the desire of the House that some things in the regulations should be omitted from the Bill. (Hear, hear.)</p>

<p>The motion of Mr. Jagger was negatived.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#henderson">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. HENDERSON</person> (Durban, Berea)</from>

<p>moved that clause 4 stand over.</p>

<p>The motion was declared carried.</p>

</speech>

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF MINES</person></from>

</speech>

<p>Keyter, Jan Gerhard.</p>
