<p>H. W. Sampson and F. H. P. Creswell, tellers.</p>

<p>The clause as amended was, therefore, agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 3,</p>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 48, to omit &#x201C;proper officer,&#x201D; and to substitute &#x201C;director.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 4, labour agents, compound managers, and conductors to be licensed,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved an amendment, which would necessitate runners being licensed or obtaining permits.</p>

<p>The amendment was adopted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved to add at the end of the clause, &#x201C;and no person shall recruit or aid in recruiting natives on ground leased by him, or in respect of which he collects rents from natives.&#x201D; The object of the amendment was to prevent undue advantage being taken of the natives. At present it often happened that natives who were in arrear with their rent were practically pressed into the service of the mines by the person entitled to collect the rent, which was unfair.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>accepted the amendment, which was agreed to</p>

<p>On clause 5, recruiting of native labourers to be under authority of licence,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 10, after &#x201C;engages&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;or recruits.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#schreiner">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. L. SCHREINER</person> (Tembuland)</from>

<p>moved: To add at the end of sub-section (a) &#x201C;ordinary industrial operations or,&#x201D; the object being to render it unnecessary for persons recruiting natives for industrial purposes to take out a licence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved an amendment: In line 10, to omit all the words from &#x201C;bona fide&#x201D; to the end of paragraph (a) and to substitute &#x201C;farming operations, domestic service, trade business, or handicraft, provided the number of natives in his employ do not at any time exceed fifty.&#x201D; He pointed out that as he read the clause, it meant that everybody who engaged natives outside of farming must have a licence.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#recruiting">

<heading>&#x201C;RECRUITING.&#x201D;</heading>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly)</from>

<p>said he did not quite catch the definition of the word &#x201C;recruiting,&#x201D; as it was not on the paper. There were about 1,500 men working on the alluvial diggings; some of these men employed one or two, or perhaps 20 boys, and as be interpreted the clause, they would be compelled to take out a licence. He thought this clause should be recast, so as not to compel these men to take out a licence. He moved to add the following amendment: &#x201C;No person shall recruit natives for employment except for his own behalf.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>hoped the Minister would allow the clause to stand down, because it wanted recasting. According to the construction of this clause it was quite possible to recruit natives for farming or any sort of employment outside the Union. He thought it would be best to delete the words &#x201C;within or outside the Union,&#x201D; and insert the words &#x201C;on any mine or works within or for any purpose whatsoever outside the Union.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>thought the clause as it stood was much better than with the amendment of the hon. member (Mr. Watt). There seemed to be some confusion between the word &#x201C;recruiting&#x201D; and &#x201C;employment.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly):</from>

<p>Could we have a definition of &#x201C;recruiting&#x201D;?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville):</from>

<p>The only accepted definition is where a man went away from his base to recruit labour.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Gape Town, Central)</from>

<p><span class="col_2249-2250" refersTo="page_1134"/>said that boys were employed for other purposes than those of the mines. What he wanted to know was if a man engaged a number of boys for work in a store or other work, would be have to take out a licence?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said it would be extremely difficult to define certain employment. If hon. members would give the Administration credit for a bit of common-sense, he would tell his hon. friend (Mr. Jagger) he could engage his natives provided he did not set up a system of touting.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#runciman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. RUNCIMAN</person> (South Peninsula)</from>

<p>said they had no objection to trusting the Administration, but they did not know what the Administration was. The Minister had just stated that the member for Cape Town could engage as many natives as he wanted provided these men came to him and offered themselves for employment. He (Mr. Runciman) might want 100 men, and would have to send to Cape Town for them. Therefore he came under the operation of this Act. He thought they ought to have the objections stated in this clause. A ship might come in requiring a couple of hundred men; was a stevedore going to take out a licence to supply these?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said it seemed to him that this Native Labour Bill was simply for the benefit of the mines. The hon. member for Cape Town (Mr. Jagger) and other hon. members were outside its scope altogether. If they were agreed on this point, what could be the objection to the amendment of the hon. member for Zoutpansberg (Mr. Mentz)?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chaplin">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. D. P. CHAPLIN</person> (Germiston)</from>

<p>said he quite agreed that those people who did not regularly recruit native labourers and did not tout for them should not be included, but he failed to see why farmers or anybody else who recruited labourers for large irrigation works should be excluded. Surely these people should be made to take out licences in the same way as persons engaged in mining and other works. He thought a great deal was to be said in favour of the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>said that the difficulty arose through the omission to describe the nature of the operations or employment in which natives were to be engaged. If the labour was for mines and works, why not say so in the clause? He hoped the Minister would allow the clause to stand down, in order to admit of its being redrafted. At present, it seemed to favour those engaged in farming operations, and so on.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>was understood to say that the regulations were to apply to organised recruiting, and he thought it would be better so far as the farming community were concerned, to leave the clause as it was.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#venter">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. A. VENTER</person> (Wodehonse)</from>

<p>said that the Bill as it stood would prevent even Divisional Councils from engaging gangs of natives to work on roads. He supported the hon. member for Zoutpansberg.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>&#x2020;The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said the Bill would be applied to the large industrial areas where they had gold and coal mines. If the amendment of the hon. member for Zoutpansberg were carried, the exemption in favour of agriculture would disappear, and the sole test would be: how many natives does a man employ?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly)</from>

<p>asked the Minister to give him an assurance that the men working on the River Diggings would not be affected. He pointed out that, as the Bill stood, a farmer might go to a kraal and get natives to dig for him, without taking out a licence; but, if he left his farm and went to dig on the River, unless natives came to him and offered their services, he could not engage them without first taking out a licence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that it was not intended to apply the regulations to a case such as had been quoted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>said that, as the clause read now, every employer of native labourers, excepting a farmer, would be required to get a recruiter&#x2019;s licence. The Minister had said that that was not the intention. He thought, the Minister should redraft the clause, so as to make it dear that it only applied to mines and works. He moved that the clause stand over so that the Minister might redraft it.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>trusted the Minister would accept the motion because the clause was very important. Agriculture was protected, but other industries should likewise receive assistance.</p>

<p>The motion was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 7, discretion as to issue, etc., of all licences,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said he would like to know on what ground it was proposed to leave it to the will of the Director to say who might or who might not be a labour agent; He maintained that there should be some right to a man to follow the occupation if he thought himself fitted for it. They should not leave it to an official to determine a man&#x2019;s qualification, so long as He bore a good character.</p>

<p>The clause was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 8,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 30, after &#x201C;licence&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;applicable to any one district.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 9,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 61 after &#x201C;licence&#x201D; <span class="col_2251-2252" refersTo="page_1135"/>to insert &#x201C;Provided that the runner may exercise his calling in any additional district if (authorised there to as prescribed.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 11, circumstances under which licences may be suspended or cancelled,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved an amendment to the effect that Magistrates, after hearing cases in connection with contravention of the regulations, should submit all papers to the Director, the latter to have power to order the licence to be cancelled or suspended. The hon. member said that it would be difficult to do the work contemplated under the Bill without contravening the regulations in some way or other. It was too severe a punishment for a man to lose his licence irrevocably. It was because the clause went too far that he had moved the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>thought that the hon. member had gone too far, and it did not necessarily follow that a man would lose his licence because he had been found guilty of a contravention of the Act. The power was left in the hands of the Minister.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>thought it was rather stiff that ta labour agent should have his licence suspended merely for getting into the hands of the police for a minor offence. Of course, what was intended was to put the power in the hands of the Minister. He, later, moved an amendment, in line 20, after the word &#x201C;offence,&#x201D; to insert the following words, &#x201C;while exercising his calling as labour agent, conductor, or runner (as the case may be).&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that the Minister was, after all, the person responsible to Parliament.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>thought that Mr. Burton had not understood the effect of the amendment.</p>

<p>Mr. Mentz&#x2019;s amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>Mr. Creswell&#x2019;s amendment was negatived.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#magistrates&#x2019;_powers">

<heading>MAGISTRATES&#x2019; POWERS</heading>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved as an amendment, to omit the words, &#x201C;may suspend the licence and,&#x201D; in line 37, and to insert &#x201C;or suspension thereof for such period,&#x201D; and to omit &#x201C;or its restoration.&#x201D; The hon. member thought they were put ting too extensive powers in the hands of the Magistrate.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said he hoped the hon. member would not press the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>supported&#x2019; the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person></from>

</speech>

<debateSection name="#contagious_diseases">

<heading>CONTAGIOUS DISEASES</heading>

<p>On clause 12, Contract of employment form and attestation,</p>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 39, to omit all the words from &#x201C;who engages&#x201D; down to &#x201C;licence&#x201D; in line 41, and to substitute &#x201C;or holder of an employer&#x2019;s licence who recruits natives,&#x201D; and to insert the following new sub-section after line 58, viz. &#x201C;(2) Every native labourer shall be registered to the person on whose behalf he is employed or recruited.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#wessels">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D. H. W. WESSELS (Bechuana-Land)</person> moved:</from>

<p>In line 46, after &#x201C;concerned; and,&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;that all recruited native labourers whose contracts are submitted for attestation have been medically examined, and are not suffering from any contagious disease, and any contract or contracts entered into with native labourers afflicted with any such disease shall be considered null and void and &#x201D;. The mover said his object was to prevent natives suffering from syphilis going to the mines.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#merriman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. X. MERRIMAN</person> (Victoria West)</from>

<p>said he entirely concurred in the scope of the amendment, but it did not go far (enough, because other diseases&#x2014;such as tuberculosis, phthisis, and heart disease&#x2014; should be included. All natives should be medically examined before their contracts were completed. He suggested the follow in amendment: &#x201C;In respect of the contract with any native, proof shall be given to the satisfaction of the attesting officer that the native attested is in sound physical health.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#smuts">

<from>&#x2020;Geneml <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. SMUTS</person> (Ermelo)</from>

<p>moved as an amendment that no native under the age of 18 years he attested. His object, he said, was to prevent the depletion of the native labour supply for farms owing to Kafirs of tender age being sent to the mines.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>hoped Mr. Wessels (would not insist on the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<p>Progress was reported, and leave obtained to sit again on Wednesday.</p>

</speech>

<heading>EVENING SITTING</heading>
